Terms of an MRQAP formula

Source: R/specify_registry.R
terms_mrqap.Rd

The terms that the right-hand side of a formula for estimate_mrqap() can name, what each one measures, and the equation of the matrix it builds. Each term builds one or more columns of the model, each a matrix with one cell for each dyad of the network. Every term is named here as it is written in a formula, such as same(x); the name of its coefficient is the name of its column, such as same_dept.

specify_mrqap(.data = net) lists the terms that suit a network, written out for its layers and node attributes (see specify_terms). A formula written for {ergm} or {goldfish} names the terms in their own way; the last section gives each term's equivalent there, and specify_mrqap() rewrites a formula from one model for another.

Notation

A cell \(x_{ij}\) of a term's matrix is for the dyad of sender (ego) \(i\) and receiver (alter) \(j\). In a two-mode network, \(i\) is a node of the first mode and \(j\) of the second. \(a_i\) is node \(i\)'s value of the attribute x, \(t_{ij}\) the value of the tie from \(i\) to \(j\) in the layer layer, and \(y_{ij}\) the value of the tie in the outcome. \(\mathbf{1}[\cdot]\) is 1 where the condition holds and 0 otherwise. In a one-mode network, the diagonal \(i = j\) is not a dyad, and is left out of the model.

Terms of node attributes

  • ego(x, levels = NULL) is the sender's value, $$x_{ij} = a_i.$$ Its column is ego_x. A categorical attribute gives one 0/1 column for each category \(c\), ego_x_c, with \(x_{ij} = \mathbf{1}[a_i = c]\), less the first category as the reference. levels = chooses the categories that get a column; the categories it leaves out are then the reference together.

  • alter(x, levels = NULL) is the receiver's value, \(x_{ij} = a_j\), as alter_x, and is dummy-coded as ego() is.

  • same(x, diff = FALSE, levels = NULL) is 1 where the sender and the receiver share a category, $$x_{ij} = \mathbf{1}[a_i = a_j],$$ as same_x. With levels =, only a category in \(L\) counts: \(x_{ij} = \mathbf{1}[a_i = a_j \in L]\). With diff = TRUE, as in ergm's nodematch(), it gives one column for each category, same_x_c, with \(x_{ij} = \mathbf{1}[a_i = a_j = c]\); a dyad of two different categories is in none of them, and is the reference. In a two-mode network, no tie joins two nodes of one mode, so same() is the share of the sender's other ties in the outcome that go to nodes like the receiver, where the attribute is only on the second mode, $$x_{ij} = \frac{\sum_{k \neq j} y_{ik} \mathbf{1}[a_k = a_j]}{\sum_{k \neq j} y_{ik}},$$ and otherwise the share of the receiver's other ties that come from nodes like the sender, $$x_{ij} = \frac{\sum_{k \neq i} y_{kj} \mathbf{1}[a_k = a_i]}{\sum_{k \neq i} y_{kj}},$$ or 0 where there is no other tie. This reads the outcome's ties.

  • mix(x, levels = NULL) gives one 0/1 column for each pair of a sender's category \(c\) and a receiver's category \(d\), mix_x_c_d, with $$x_{ij} = \mathbf{1}[a_i = c,\ a_j = d],$$ less the first pair as the reference. In an undirected network the pair is unordered, and \(x_{ij}\) is also 1 where \(a_i = d\) and \(a_j = c\). The pairs are in ergm's order for nodemix(), the sender's category changing fastest, and levels = names a pair as "c -> d", or "c -- d" where it is unordered.

  • diff(x, transformer_fn = abs) is the transformed difference between the sender's and the receiver's values, $$x_{ij} = f(a_i - a_j),$$ as diff_x: the absolute difference \(|a_i - a_j|\) by default, and the signed difference with transformer_fn = identity.

  • sim(x) is the similarity of the two values, as a share of the largest difference between any sender and receiver, $$x_{ij} = 1 - \frac{|a_i - a_j|}{\max_{kl} |a_k - a_l|},$$ as sim_x. In a one-mode network, the largest difference is the range of the attribute.

same(), same(diff = TRUE), and mix() of one attribute measure its homophily in different ways, as diff() and sim() do, so a model takes one of each. diff() and sim() need a numeric attribute. match(x) is a deprecated alias of same(x, diff = TRUE), and dist(x) of diff(x).

Terms of other layers

These read another layer of a multiplex network, or a tie attribute, and refuse the outcome's own layer, since they would predict the outcome's ties from those same ties.

  • tie(layer, weighted = FALSE) is 1 where the layer has a tie, $$x_{ij} = \mathbf{1}[t_{ij} > 0],$$ or its value, \(x_{ij} = t_{ij}\), with weighted = TRUE, as tie_layer. A layer named on its own enters with its values as stored, as layer.

  • exchange(layer, weighted = NULL) is the reverse tie, $$x_{ij} = t_{ji},$$ as exchange_layer, with its values as stored; \(\mathbf{1}[t_{ji} > 0]\) with weighted = FALSE. recip(layer) is the same, as recip_layer.

  • indeg(layer, node = "alter", weighted = FALSE) is the receiver's number of incoming ties, \(x_{ij} = \sum_{k} w_{kj}\), as indeg_layer, or the sender's with node = "ego", \(x_{ij} = \sum_{k} w_{ki}\), as ego_indeg_layer.

  • outdeg(layer, node = "ego", weighted = FALSE) is the sender's number of outgoing ties, \(x_{ij} = \sum_{k} w_{ik}\), as ego_outdeg_layer, or the receiver's with node = "alter", \(x_{ij} = \sum_{k} w_{jk}\), as outdeg_layer.

In the degrees, \(w_{kl} = \mathbf{1}[t_{kl} > 0]\), or \(t_{kl}\) with weighted = TRUE; a loop \(k = l\) and an unobserved tie are not counted. In a two-mode network only the second mode receives and only the first sends, so indeg(node = "ego") and outdeg(node = "alter") abort. type = is a deprecated alias of node =, and goldfish's name for it. goldfish reads the receiver for both, so a formula written for goldfish is read as goldfish reads it, and goldfish's indeg or outdeg on its own, the outcome's own degree, is dropped.

Terms of others' attributes

  • tertius(layer, x, summarizer_fn = "mean") is the mean value of the receiver's other in-neighbours in the layer: the nodes \(k\), other than the sender, with a tie to the receiver, $$x_{ij} = \frac{1}{|N_{ij}|} \sum_{k \in N_{ij}} a_k, \quad N_{ij} = \{k \neq i : t_{kj} > 0\},$$ as tertius_layer_x (Haunss and Hollway 2023). A node \(k\) with no value is left out of \(N_{ij}\), and where \(N_{ij}\) is empty, \(x_{ij}\) is the mean of the other cells. With summarizer_fn = "sum", it is the sum weighted by the tie's value, \(x_{ij} = \sum_{k \neq i} t_{kj} a_k\).

  • tertius_diff(layer, x, summarizer_fn = "mean") is how far the sender's value lies from that mean, $$x_{ij} = \left|a_i - \frac{1}{|N_{ij}|} \sum_{k \in N_{ij}} a_k\right|,$$ as tertius_diff_layer_x, and is filled in the same way.

Both need a numeric attribute. tertius(x) without a layer reads the outcome's own ties, and warns.

Terms of the outcome's previous wave

On a longitudinal network, these read the outcome in the wave before, \(y^{(w-1)}\), as goldfish and RSiena read the network before each change. On a network of one wave, they could only read the outcome's own ties, so inertia and trans are dropped, and recip warns.

  • inertia is 1 where the tie was there in the wave before, $$x_{ij} = \mathbf{1}[y^{(w-1)}_{ij} > 0],$$ or its value with inertia(weighted = TRUE).

  • recip is the reverse tie in the wave before, \(x_{ij} = y^{(w-1)}_{ji}\).

  • trans is the number of two-paths from the sender to the receiver in the wave before, $$x_{ij} = \sum_{k} b_{ik} b_{kj}, \quad b_{kl} = \mathbf{1}[y^{(w-1)}_{kl} > 0],$$ where an unobserved tie counts as 0.

Terms of a list of networks

  • global(x) is a variable \(g_m\) of the whole network \(m\), from its globals, for every dyad of that network: \(x_{ij} = g_m\), as global_x. On one network it is the intercept, so it needs a list of networks.

Terms of the reporter of a cognitive social structure

A cognitive social structure (CSS) holds each reporter \(r\)'s report of the network, so each cell is \(x_{ijr}\), for the dyad as \(r\) reports it (Krackhardt 1987).

  • reporter(x, levels = NULL) is the reporter's value, \(x_{ijr} = a_r\), as reporter_x, and is dummy-coded as ego() is.

  • reporter_ego is 1 where the reporter is the sender, \(x_{ijr} = \mathbf{1}[r = i]\), and reporter_alter where the reporter is the receiver, \(x_{ijr} = \mathbf{1}[r = j]\): a report of the reporter's own ties.

  • reporter_same(x, node = "ego") is 1 where the reporter shares the sender's category, \(x_{ijr} = \mathbf{1}[a_r = a_i]\), as reporter_same_ego_x, or the receiver's with node = "alter", \(x_{ijr} = \mathbf{1}[a_r = a_j]\).

See the section on cognitive social structures in estimate_mrqap().

Choosing categories with levels =

levels = chooses the categories that get a column in ego(), alter(), and same(), or the pairs in mix(), as in ergm. Give the names, such as levels = c("sales", "hr") or, for mix(), levels = "sales -> hr", written as in fit$terms (-- for an undirected network). Or give positions in the order of the columns, where a negative position leaves that one out: levels = -1 is the default of ego(), alter(), and mix(). In ego(), alter(), and mix(), the categories left out are the reference together; where every one is chosen, the first chosen is the reference. In same(), a dyad that shares a category left out is not counted. An unknown name aborts and lists the categories. A term with more than ten categories and no levels = warns, since under permute = "predictor" each column is permuted on its own.

Interactions

: and * give interactions of any order. An interaction is the product of its terms' cells, \(x_{ij} = x^{(1)}_{ij} x^{(2)}_{ij}\), with one column for each pair of their columns, named by joining their names with :, such as ego_age:same_office.

Equivalents in other models

A formula written for {ergm} or {goldfish} can be used as it is, and specify_mrqap() and specify_ergm() rewrite a formula for each other's model. The nearest term of each is:

infernetergmgoldfishRSiena
ego(x)nodeocov("x"), nodeofactor("x"); b1cov("x") in a two-mode network; nodecov("x") in an undirected oneego(x)egoX
alter(x)nodeicov("x"), nodeifactor("x"); b2cov("x") in a two-mode networkalter(x)altX
same(x)nodematch("x")same(x)sameX
same(x, diff = TRUE)nodematch("x", diff = TRUE)
mix(x)nodemix("x")
ego(x, levels = ), same(x, levels = )nodeofactor("x", levels = ), nodematch("x", levels = )
mix(x, levels = )nodemix("x", levels2 = )
diff(x)absdiff("x")diff(x)absDiffX
diff(x, transformer_fn = identity)diff("x")diff(x, transformer_fn = identity)diffX
sim(x)edgecov()sim(x), as minus the absolute differencesimX, centred
a layer, or tie(layer)edgecov()tie(layer)X
exchange(layer)edgecov() of the transposerecip(layer)
indeg(layer), outdeg(layer)edgecov()indeg(layer), outdeg(layer, type = "ego")
tertius(layer, x), tertius_diff(layer, x)edgecov()the same, with the sender among the in-neighbours
global(x)global(x)
recipmutualreciprecip
inertiainertia
transttripletranstransTrip

sim() is on another scale in goldfish, which changes its coefficient but not its test, and goldfish's tertius() counts the sender among the in-neighbours, so specify_mrqap() names both where it reads a goldfish formula. ergm's edges is the intercept, which an MRQAP always has. The reporter terms have no equivalent, since no other model has a reporter. ergm's terms of the outcome's own structure, such as gwesp(), and goldfish's endogenous effects, such as cycle, have no MRQAP term, and an MRQAP drops them (see specify).

References

Haunss, Sebastian, and James Hollway. 2023. "Multimodal mechanisms of political discourse dynamics and the case of Germany's nuclear energy phase-out." Network Science 11(2): 205-223. doi:10.1017/nws.2022.31 .

Krackhardt, David. 1987. "Cognitive Social Structures." Social Networks 9(2): 109-134. doi:10.1016/0378-8733(87)90009-8 .

Morris, Martina, Mark S. Handcock, and David R. Hunter. 2008. "Specification of Exponential-Family Random Graph Models: Terms and Computational Aspects." Journal of Statistical Software 24(4): 1-24. doi:10.18637/jss.v024.i04 .

See also

estimate_mrqap() fits a formula of these terms; specify_terms lists the terms that suit a network.

Other models: control_mrqap(), diagnose_confusion(), other_results, play_diffusions(), print.netreg_lm(), regression, specify, specify_terms, test_fit, test_measures, test_parameter()

Examples

# Every term that suits a network, and the columns of some of them
specify_mrqap(advice ~ ., manynet::ison_lawfirm)
